nodes.title: Residue towers of higher local fields
nodes.statement: An n-local field is a tower F_n=F,F_{n-1},…,F_0, with each F_i (i>0) a complete discrete valuation field, a specified residue-field isomorphism κ(F_i)≃F_{i-1}, and F_0 finite. Store the valuations, completeness witnesses and residue identifications as coherent data. The one-local comparison identifies this with the ordinary nonarchimedean local-field interface once the chosen valuation and topology agree.
hypotheses: n≥0. A finite field is zero-local. The first residue field is F_{n-1}, the last F_0.

Specifying a tower does not assert the existence of several inequivalent complete discrete valuations on the same field. Coordinates depend on parameters; the successive residue-field description is intrinsic up to its canonical comparisons.
proofSteps: Import the complete DVR and one-local interface from LFR.0. Define the finite indexed tower and its truncation maps; transport along field isomorphisms compatible with valuations.
Prove the one-step residue recursion and the one-local comparison. Separate parameter choices and rank valuation into their own targets.

nodes.title: Mixed series fields

hypotheses: E carries its specified complete discrete valuation; convergence in the negative exponent direction is essential.
proofSteps: Show convolution converges using the boundedness and negative-tail conditions; use leading reduction modulo a uniformizer to prove multiplicativity of the minimum valuation.

nodes.title: Higher additive topologies
nodes.statement: Construct higher additive topologies recursively. On E((T)), neighborhoods of zero are boxes Σ_i U_iT^i with each U_i an open zero-neighborhood of E and U_i=E for all sufficiently large i. On E{{T}}, use boxes with U_i open zero-neighborhoods satisfying two different conditions: some outer valuation ideal m_E^c is contained in every U_i; for every integer r, m_E^r is contained in U_i for all sufficiently large i. Eventual equality U_i=E is not required in this mixed-series case. Transport to finite extensions through a coefficient-vector basis. Addition and multiplication by a fixed nonzero scalar are continuous; for n>1 multiplication need not be jointly continuous.
hypotheses: Finite last residue field. Equal characteristic uses the canonical coefficient lifts. When the first residue has characteristic zero, the topology may depend on a coefficient-field section; keep that choice explicit.
Mixed fields with first residue of positive characteristic have the canonical topology of Morrow Theorem 4.8. Do not give a global topological-field instance.
proofSteps: Use the coefficient boxes specified in the fine HL.0 component for equal-series steps; prove invariance in the positive-characteristic case by parameter substitutions.

For mixed series use the common contained valuation ideal and the eventual containment of every valuation ideal to control multiplication by a fixed scalar. Compare two finite-extension bases by linear changes of coordinates.
Separate raw higher topology from sequential saturation and the categorical finite-index openness in HL.3. Source-level invariance inputs are G01 and G02.

nodes.statement: Assume NonarchimedeanAddGroup K. The identity map from K((T)) with its native outer T-adic topology to higherTopology(K) is continuous. In Mathlib topology order this says outerTopology ≤ higherTopology.
hypotheses: K is a field with a specified topology; K((T)) is the native LaurentSeries carrier. Additional topological hypotheses are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: It suffices to compare neighborhoods of zero in the two additive groups. Any higher neighborhood contains an admissible box with cutoff N.
The tail lemma puts T^N K[[T]] inside that box. The native Laurent-series valuation inequality identifies the tail with v(f)≤exp(−N).
A strictly smaller native valuation ball lies inside this tail, so the box is an outer zero-neighborhood. Translate to all points.
acceptance: The direction reverses the inherited packet assertion. A sequence converging in the outer topology converges in the higher topology.

nodes.title: Equality of the two topologies detects discrete coefficients
nodes.statement: Assume NonarchimedeanAddGroup K. The higher topology on K((T)) equals the native outer T-adic topology if and only if the topology of K is discrete.
hypotheses: K is a field with a specified topology; K((T)) is the native LaurentSeries carrier. Additional topological hypotheses are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: If K is discrete, the coefficient family {0} for i<N and K for i≥N is admissible and its box is T^N K[[T]]. Thus each native valuation neighborhood contains a higher neighborhood. Combine with the comparison theorem.
Conversely, the topology that the outer valuation induces on constants is discrete: the outer open ball T K[[T]] meets constants only in zero.

The induced-single theorem identifies the topology on constants in the higher topology with the original topology of K. Equality therefore forces zero to be open, hence all singletons to be open by translation.
acceptance: A finite discrete residue field gives the ordinary one-dimensional Laurent-series topology. An inner Laurent-series field with its valuation topology gives strict inequality.

It is not enough merely to test the outer first residue F_{n−1} when n>2. If F_1 has characteristic zero, ordinary one-local duality permits its residue prime at the bottom step.

The Milnor search hit PR 44404 on sigma-locally-finite families, not K-theory. Targeted public Zulip-archive searches found the March 2024 ramification discussion (https://leanprover-community.github.io/archive/stream/113489-new-members/topic/preimage.20of.20quotient.20galois.20group.html), which emphasizes ordinary discrete-valuation scope and conventional lower/upper numbering. researchNotes.title: Independent implementation leads
researchNotes.statement: The external NYLL source at commit 431143bad96b10a8f80381346ed1631ce463b055 defines ValuationTheory.IsHigherLocalField by actual complete-DVR residue recursion and proves finite-extension permanence (https://github.com/n-yamaguchi-0729/NYLL/blob/431143bad96b10a8f80381346ed1631ce463b055/Nyll/Yamaguchi26AbfaithfulGalois/HigherLocalField/Basic.lean). Basic, PositiveCharacteristic and Properties were read as design references. This is an existential predicate over NYLL CompleteDVF, whereas the target here carries a compatible chosen tower and topology; no equivalence to the pinned native carriers is presumed. Its imported dependency graph has not been audited or elaborated at the pins. Robin Carlier’s KMilnorWitt project (https://github.com/robin-carlier/KMilnorWitt) formalizes Milnor–Witt ring presentations; its README lists ordinary Milnor K as a further quotient still to construct. These are independent implementation leads, not baseline declarations. No code is integrated or copied; any proposed port requires author coordination and a license/interface audit.
